pillarForecast.why: In A the late field is unchanged, so pursuers still 'auto-die' on rocks when he reaches sectors 5-6; B should feel more like his own doing, but only on runs that get that far.
Slow-mo in every run keeps the earned breather; more lasers add peaks he can read.

Lasers every 3.8s in Breakout on top of five pursuers and two chargers: expect at least one 'didn't see that laser' death late in a run, mostly in B where fewer rocks crowd the view but more pressure falls on him.
Nothing new appears in the world in this build and he has already won from sector 1; with the core declared complete, 'what moves me forward between runs' becomes the open itch (meta loop).
A may still draw 'too easy' at the end; B and the extra lasers may fix it, so it splits by variant.
No new inputs; controls stay silent.

biggestRisk: Novelty exhaustion, not a mechanic: the only changes live in sectors 5-6, which he reaches on maybe half his runs, and he already called the core loop complete and won from sector 1. With nothing new to discover and no reason to play beyond the run itself, enthusiasm decays into 'still fun, but what am I playing for' and a meh or two late in the session (run 16 pattern: a 'no' after winning), with his comments turning to the meta loop instead of the tuning.
abVerdict: Leans B, weakly, and mostly unnamed (~55% he never names the rock difference; the extra lasers in both variants get noticed first). If he names it, it will be B framed in his own run-58 terms ('I had to lure them myself at the end', 'less auto-die'), or an A run drawing 'the end is still easy, too many rocks'. Small chance (~15%) he calls B's ending empty or too hard with all the lasers.
